predictions.text: New York Rangers to beat Los Angeles at Madison Square Garden. The Rangers are a perfect 6-0-0 at home, outscoring visitors 29-10, although they arrive on a two-game losing run. The Kings are 2-5-2, have scored only 21 goals in nine games while allowing 32, and the NHL schedule has them in Chicago the following night. We set the Rangers at 70%, a fair -229.

predictions.text: Anaheim Ducks to beat Vancouver at Honda Center. Vancouver are 2-10-1 with 60 goals against in 13 games and have taken one point from their last ten (0-9-1), the current skid running to four. Anaheim's own home form is weak at 1-3-0, which is the reason the number stops at -222 (69%) instead of going shorter.

audit.text: The front-door banner is a hard-coded paragraph about the 25 October desk, including literal counts ("Nine fixtures", "three graded picks"). Nothing ties those words to data/a394f91e/desk.json, so they go stale the moment a new desk lands. This desk repoints the banner, but the text is still literal.

The banner says "the twelve with no priced match". The a394f91e desk priced two sports (basketball and ice hockey), which leaves thirteen, and its own flag F22 says fourteen. Three different numbers describe the same desk.

Flag F22 of the 25 October desk opens "Fourteen of the fifteen brief sports have no priced match" and then says "for thirteen sports" in the same sentence. Only thirteen is consistent with its fixtures.

The canonical summary hard-codes "Six high-confidence picks are live for the next two days" and "ice hockey and baseball" next to computed KPIs. The cron in current-pages.yml rebuilds this page every three hours, so the sentence can contradict the KPI tiles directly under it.
ARCHIVE labels carry literal counts ("9 official fixtures ... 22 flags"). They are never reconciled with the desk data they describe.
archive_panel silently drops any ARCHIVE entry whose file is missing (`if (ROOT / d).is_file()`), so a typo in a desk path removes it from the front door without any error.
The artifact copy loop also skips missing desk folders with `continue`. Combined with the line above, a broken ARCHIVE entry fails silently in both places.

validate_desk only walks manifest["pages"], the root pages. Desk subfolders such as a394f91e/ are copied into the artifact but never checked for broken links, missing sources or empty tables by the canonical gate; each desk relies on its own optional script.
The unregistered-HTML check globs only site/*.html, so stray pages inside desk subfolders are never caught.
CI runs `python -m pipeline.refresh` against live sites before building, so the same commit can build different pages depending on which publishers answer within 10 seconds.

PUBLISHERS, which feeds OFFICIAL_HOSTS in pipeline/validate.py line 161, lists www.legavolley.it (the men's Lega Pallavolo) but not legavolleyfemminile.it, and no German ice hockey host such as penny-del.org. Women's Serie A1 and DEL rows could not pass the canonical source check even when the link is the official league page.

79 eight-character session folders contain an index.html but only 20 of them are registered in ARCHIVE. The other 59 (for example 0c9bc692/, 1707d752/, 2360a617/) are committed but are neither copied into the Pages artifact nor linked from the front door.

The peer 26 October desk (103ea76b, merged as PR #300 while this desk was being built) prices World Series Game 5 and grades Tampa Bay +1.5 High at -167. The official MLB schedule marks Game 5 "if necessary"; Milwaukee lead 2-0, so the game only happens if Tampa Bay win at least once first. The conditional status is not shown next to the pick.
Games 3, 4 and 5 on that desk carry the identical probability (0.625908) and price, so the published Game 3 probable starters (Gasser and Peralta, both on the official feed) do not enter its price.

NBA picks there are graded High (for example Oklahoma City -177) on fixtures whose start time is blank because no official schedule was readable; fixture existence rests on the OLBG listing plus the NBA standings. This desk read the same gap and issued no basketball pick.
The baseball page says "No price today" directly above a picks table that lists a priced World Series pick.
